notes: Thirteen pairs around the Starlight keeper, the Banisher monk, Arrow, and Hornet, tying the quiet heavy hitters and the low-flying farmers into the existing company.

C.title: Night watch
beats: Dray lights the Starlight at dusk out of habit. Kettle is sitting under it with a thermos and a flak chart.
That beam is a lamp with opinions.
It was a lamp. I kept the habit and lost the ships.
Then we're in the same trade. Keeping the dark honest.

B.title: Two shifts
beats: They split the night. Dray sweeps the ridge, Kettle sweeps the cloud deck, and neither wakes the other.
Three crows and a rumour. You?
A fox. It's a better class of company than the rumour.

A.title: The long sweep
beats: A raider came in under the cloud and ran straight into the beam, and the Archangel finished what the light began.
You held it still for me.
I held it still for forty years. Nobody ever thanked the ship for crashing elsewhere.
I'll say it for the ship.

C.title: Lamp and kiln
beats: The Kiln walks past the Starlight at the pace of a funeral. Dray turns the beam to follow him and thinks better of it.
It was never meant to. It was meant to be seen from far away.
I'd rather be felt from near.

B.title: Slow against slow
beats: Both are plodders, and both resent being passed by anything with wheels.
I arrive in my own time.
I arrive in yours. The turret you're aiming at has already stopped existing.
Then we'll agree on one thing. Nobody asked it to stay.

A.title: Heat and clearance
beats: The beam pinned the bunker's gun crew. The Kiln walked in afterwards and had nothing left to argue with.
I lit the door. You are the one who went through.
Keep your lamp. I'll keep my walk.

motifs: reach of light against a turret ring

C.title: Whose circle
beats: Warder's chalk ring and the Starlight's sweep overlap by about a hundred paces of nothing.
That ground is where the light lands.

B.title: Overlap
beats: A scout crossed into the overlap. Both of them fired, and the scout's apology reached no one.
My Thistles were already tracking it.
Then it died of too much supervision.

A.title: Shared boundary
beats: Warder moved a marker stone ten paces. Dray didn't mention it, and swept a little wider to cover the gap.
A circle needs something to be outside of.

C.title: The same hush
beats: Two heavy hitters sit on the same ridge for an hour. Neither has said a word and both consider it a good conversation.
Some things aren't ready until they're quiet.

B.title: Before the verse
beats: The Banishers are loaded. The Starlight is warming. Neither side will go first, out of courtesy.
The verse is mine to begin.
The light is mine to end.
A monastery would have called that a liturgy.

A.title: Amen
beats: The volley fell, the beam swept after, and the ridge was left very still.
I'll speak of it. In about thirty years, to a fox.
Then it will be told correctly.

motifs: faith that lands and faith that grows

C.title: Two faiths
beats: Lumen tithes heat into the pad. Brother Ansel watches the Prudes bloom and says nothing, loudly.
I disapprove of faith that needs watering.
Mine is geothermal. It waters itself.

B.title: Harvest and verse
beats: Ansel's volley cleared a hillside. Lumen's garden had already planted a Pulsar on the crater's lip.
You leave room. I fill it.
I leave silence. You fill that, too.

A.title: Grace, both kinds
beats: The garden held the line until the Banishers found their range. Neither pretended afterwards to have won alone.
Your faith stayed where it stood.
Yours never stays anywhere. It only arrives.
I will not call it holy. I will say it was needed.

C.title: Two captains
beats: Quill marches the Bulls past the Banishers at inspection. Ansel does not look up from his rosary.
A captain faces the target. The line learns by watching the target vanish.

B.title: Order of fire
beats: Quill wants the Bulls forward before the volley. Ansel wants the volley before anyone moves.
My order lands. Yours would walk into it.

A.title: Chain of command
beats: The battery fired and the Bulls advanced into the silence it left. The timing was exact, and neither of them admitted it was agreed.
Do not mistake that for approval.

C.title: Before the shot
beats: Two heavy artillery heroes stand ten paces apart, both waiting. One is praying and one is waiting for a scout.
I need to be shown it first.
So we both wait on something we can't order.

B.title: Reading the map
beats: The Augur paints a target. Ansel bows his head. Lund checks the Rascals' report for the third time.
Only because someone else saw for me. You know the arrangement.
It's my arrangement too. I just keep it in writing.

A.title: Signature and verse
beats: The Tremor rearranged the valley with her signature. The Banishers added the afterword.

motifs: the list of those who walked away
the shot that is a fact

C.title: Short lists
beats: Venn's list is pinned inside the Arrow hatch. Yeva's ghosts are somewhere out in the fog, leaving no list at all.
Everyone I've missed is on that paper.
Everyone I've missed was never there.
That's either a lie or a very good shot.

B.title: Patience compared
beats: They lay up on the same ridge for six hours. At hour five, both of them noticed the same wolf.
Mine either. We have a lot of standards.

A.title: Fact and question
beats: The first Arrow shot asked. The second shot, from Yeva's lane, answered.
I told. Shall we split the credit?
I'll take the list. You can have the silence.

C.title: Out loud
beats: Verse counts her Javelins from twelve to one. Venn counts nothing, and has opinions about people who do.
Each missile is a word. I say them all.

B.title: Zero
beats: Verse reached zero. Something died. Venn wrote nothing down.
Zero, again. You don't want to say it?
I don't count the ones that don't walk away.
That's the cruellest thing anyone's said about my arithmetic.

A.title: Sums
beats: Verse's last missile and Venn's second arrow hit the same man. He had been on the list for two weeks.
Counting is my job. I'll strike him in the ledger and you can keep the paper.
Good. I'm not sure which of us was first.

C.title: No hurry
beats: Kit has already set fire to the target. Venn is still lining up the first shot.
It's burning in the wrong place.
Then it's a very pretty wrong place.

B.title: Wait for it
beats: Venn made Kit sit for forty minutes on the same ridge. Kit's Belchers did not ignite once.
I think my hands are asleep.
That's the first thing you've held still.
Is this what it's like inside your head? Dull?

A.title: Question and flame
beats: The first Arrow shot pinned the commander. Kit walked in and gave him something worth looking at.
I waited for the question. I'm so proud I could burst.

motifs: low over flat ground, low over water
both come back for the rest

C.title: Flat things
beats: Marsh complains that the war is flat. Gale points out that, at least, hers is wet.
Nothing to land on, except water.
That's the opposite problem, and it's yours.

B.title: Second pass
beats: Both wings took the same road: sting on the first pass, wait for the dust, return on the second.
I always come back. You do too.
Have to. It's rude to leave a nest half-eaten.

A.title: Rain on the field
beats: A storm flooded the flat ground Marsh hated. Her Hornets lifted off the fields while the Cutlasses settled on the new lake.
You made the war less flat.
I made a pond. Come and see what it grows.

motifs: a scout who sees by hurting

C.title: Scars on the map
beats: Volt's Jaguars have burned a line across the ridge. Marsh flies along it the way you'd follow a furrow.
That's a plough line. Thank you.

B.title: Stung and scarred
beats: Volt lights a column. Marsh dives on the burning end. Neither asked for the other's permission.
You came in the moment I lit it.
You made it easy to find the corner of the field.
I'm not used to being useful and fast.

A.title: Eyes and sting
beats: The Jaguars painted the target and the Hornets did the rest. The enemy regrouped around nothing.
